the 657delT mutation is a risk factor for sporadic lymphoid neoplasms in the Polish population, but not for Hodgkin lymphoma, and that it is not a major genetic factor for childhood lymphoid malignancy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency of NBS1 mutation carriers is increased among children with sporadic ALL or NHL, but not among those with Hodgkin lymphomas.
the 657del 5 mutation in NBS1 is not a major cause of sporadic childhood and adolescence non‐Hodkin lymphomas.
the NBS1 mutation carriers are not a major risk for the development of childhood and adolescent lymphoid malignancies but the risk is still higher than that in the general population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency of NBS1 657del5 is higher in patients with lymphoid malignancies compared with healthy controls.
heterozygosity for the 657delT mutation of the NBS1 (Nijmegen break syndrome 1) gene is not a major genetic risk factor for the development of childhood and adolescent sporadic lymphoid tumors.
